$comment: A Kleopatra keyring of Satoshi-impersonation keys, transcribed from a screenshot. UNTRUSTED, image-transcribed. Key ID column shows the 64-bit long key id. Includes the ONE genuine key (18C09E865EC948A1, DSA, 2008-10-30) surrounded by forgeries: short-id collisions on 5EC948A1 and keys whose UIDs are free-text impersonations. Used by spa.analysis.keyid_collision. 'certified' here is a LOCAL trust marking, not third-party proof.

entries.label: BuZz Spacedout
entries.note: Short-ID-collision forgery confirmed by full fingerprint: only the last 32 bits (5EC948A1) match the genuine key DE4E...48A1; the other 32 hex chars differ. RSA-1024, claims 2018 (not backdated), private key n/a.

entries.label: Satoshi Nakamoto (M is the real Satoshi)
entries.note: Pure NAMESQUAT forgery (user-created demonstration). Correct name + email + plausible 2008 date + non-anachronistic RSA-2048, and a working private key on the creator's machine - but does NOT even collide the short id (D15AB5BC vs 5EC948A1) and the full fingerprint 9932...B5BC shares nothing with the genuine DE4E...48A1. Proves that UID text and 'certified' status are attacker-controlled; only the full fingerprint defeats it.

entries.label: Satoshi Nakamoto (This is a demonstration key to prove forging is possible...M)
